label: FortiSwitch 108F-FPOE 8-port desktop PoE switch (130 W)
description: Fortinet FortiSwitch 108F-FPOE fanless desktop Layer 2 PoE switch: 8x GE RJ45 all 802.3af/at PSE (130 W budget), 2x 1G SFP, 20 Gbps switching capacity, 30 Mpps.

poe.note: 8 PoE ports, 130 W total (datasheet). 130 W covers eight Class 3 (802.3af, 15.4 W) devices at 123.2 W but only four Class 4 (802.3at, 30 W) devices at 120 W: 8 x 30 W = 240 W is not available, so the 30 W per-port ceiling is a port capability, not a promise to all eight at once. Internal AC supply, 100-240 V, 1.4 A max, 139.2 W consumption fully loaded.

fabric.note: Datasheet switching capacity 20 Gbps duplex with 30 Mpps: 2 x 10 Gbit/s, the line rate of eight 1G RJ45 ports plus two 1G SFP cages.

notes: Datasheet: 8x GE RJ45 and 2x GE SFP; 8 (802.3af/at) PoE ports, 130 W budget; 20 Gbps switching capacity, 30 Mpps, 8 K MAC, 4 us latency, 4 K VLANs, 512 KB packet buffer, 256 MB DDR3, 32 MB flash, >10 years MTBF. 44 x 209 x 250 mm, 1.84 kg, fanless, desktop or 19-inch bracket. All eight copper ports are PSE ports; the two SFP cages are not. The PoE MAX LED reads 130 W on the front panel (108F QuickStart Guide). FortiLink ports 7-10. Console is the RJ-45 serial port, FortiSwitchOS default 115200 8-N-1 (https://docs.fortinet.com/document/fortiswitch/7.6.5/enterprise-data-center-switching-with-evpn-vxlan-deployment-guide/313313/deployment-procedures), console default IP 192.168.1.99. Layer 2 only - routing is the FortiGate's job over FortiLink. The FS-108F-POE was left out of this batch: the datasheet table says 8 PoE ports while Fortinet's own switch page says 4, and no vendor document settles which of its eight ports source power.
